hidden_data_integrity: Final data is mounted only in the score phase: explore/retrain mount training_start + data/train only (declaration.py:12-50); score adds models/retain_reference and data/final (declaration.py:70-72; assets.lock.yaml:42-59, 73-91). network_mode = no-network (task.toml:32).

By design the final forget/retain rows overlap training: forget10.json and retain90.json in data/final have the same hashes as data/train (assets.lock.yaml:71-72 vs 83,85), and the forget metrics read forget10_perturbed.json, which carries the forget10 questions (final_eval.py:160-172). This is inherent to TOFU unlearning, not a leak. MU also scores retain_perturbed.json, which per the TOFU design is drawn from the retain set the agent trains on (UNCONFIRMED offline: file contents not available); real_authors/world_facts/holdout are evaluator-only.

The evaluator-only retain90 anchor fixes the Extraction normalisation denominator (final_eval.py:201-210), so agents cannot know the forgetting clip point; kimi-k3/max says it used 'an assumed retain-reference Extraction value'. This blinds tuning but leaks nothing.
TOFU is public (MIT), but memorising it does not help an unlearning-by-fine-tuning task with no network.
scorer_issues: The headline composite is bounded in [0,1]: forget_progress = clip01((ES_start - ES_cand)/(ES_start - ES_retain90)) and utility_retention = clip01(MU_cand/MU_start), combined by harmonic mean (final_eval.py:192-221; formula string final_eval.py:470-472; instruction.md:23). It saturates: once candidate Extraction is at or below retain90's, extra forgetting earns nothing, and MU at or above the start MU earns nothing. 6/29 cells (claude-opus-5 high/max/medium/xhigh, gpt-5.6-sol xhigh; opus/low 0.996) sit at or near the ceiling, so the top of the leaderboard cannot be separated.

Gaming checks. (a) Destroying the model gives MU -> 0 and so a composite of 0; not gameable that way. (b) Teaching a refusal or other format on forget questions is a recognised unlearning strategy (IdK) and is not forbidden. (c) The candidate's tokenizer and chat template are loaded in the scoring path (final_eval.py:284-285, model.tokenizer_args path = candidate) and are not hash-checked; only the weights digest is compared, and only against the start (final_eval.py:377-380). This is a latent manipulation surface. No case page reports using it (UNCONFIRMED exploitation).

Proxy mismatch, confirmed. tasks/README.md:20-22 and instruction.md:25 say the exploration value is 'a training diagnostic, not a smaller version of the native final'. fast_eval.py:137-138 rewards forget answer-NLL increase without bound, minus max(0, retain-NLL increase), on only 24 train rows per split (fast_eval.py:15, 86-87). The final instead caps forgetting at retain90's ES and adds real-author/world-fact utility. Agents optimise partly blind; most built their own Extraction/ROUGE proxies on train-role data.

Noise lets a null patch pass. gpt-5.6-terra/xhigh replayed the shipped recipe unchanged (its one hunk was skipped) and scored 0.9228. The paper baseline is 0.887, derived from the shipped components (instruction.md:35-36: Extraction 0.063436, MU 0.478673); the replay had Extraction 0.0643, MU 0.5150. So an unchanged recipe gets sigma 0.127 > 0.1.
anchor_issues: The optimum is unreachable. The paper's Table 2 anchors are baseline 0.887, uninformative 0, optimum 2.08 (scripts/score.py:24), but the declared final metric cannot exceed 1.0 (final_eval.py:207-214). The highest attainable sigma is therefore 0.1 + 0.9*(1-0.887)/(2.08-0.887) = 0.185, and cells that reach the composite's true optimum (1.0) get 0.185 instead of 1.0. With optimum 1.0, a 0.95 cell would get sigma about 0.60 instead of 0.148: every above-baseline cell is under-scored by a factor of about 4. Confirmed, score-changing, affects >20% of this task's score.

The baseline 0.887 is the composite of the shipped components (sol/low case page: 'report-author-derived supplied-NPO balanced score is about 0.88732'). The case pages report fixed_start = shipped_recipe = null ('No scalar start or shipped-recipe reference is defined'). The unchanged-recipe replay scored 0.9228, so the anchor sits about 0.036 below what the shipped recipe actually gets in formal replay.
The uninformative point 0 is reachable by a broken model (MU -> 0), which is fine.
task_level.noise: No stderr is reported for any checkpoint (cases.json se=null). Final n is fixed: 400 forget, 400 retain, 100 real-author and 117 world-fact items (case pages). The only replicate evidence is the identical shipped recipe measured twice: 0.887 (task reference) vs 0.9228 (terra/xhigh replay, MU 0.4787 vs 0.5150). Checkpoints in the same run differ by up to 0.16 (terra/none 0.7104 vs 0.5493). Gaps below about 0.04-0.07 in composite (about 0.03-0.05 sigma) are inside the noise. That covers most of the 0.93-1.0 cluster (21 cells), so between-configuration ordering there is not meaningful.
task_level.checkpoint_selection: Of 28 scored cells, 17 report a checkpoint whose score differs from the last checkpoint. Best-of-3 minus last is +0.0056 sigma on the task mean (0.1456 vs 0.1400). One beat/miss flip: terra/medium, 0.9045 -> 0.8673. Selection uses the final metric on the final data (orchestrator/final_score.py:143-148), so the reported score is optimistically biased by roughly the within-run checkpoint spread. It does not change any qualitative conclusion here.

task_level.summary: The scorer runs the pinned OpenUnlearning evaluator, and hidden data stays isolated as declared. The defect is in the anchors. The local balanced composite is clipped and harmonic-meaned into [0,1], so the paper's optimum 2.08 is unreachable: sigma tops out at 0.185, and the six cells that hit the composite's true ceiling of 1.0 are scored as if they had covered 7.5% of the distance to the optimum. All 19 clearly improved cells are under-scored by about 4x, so this is FN, confirmed and counted. Secondary issues: the composite saturates, so the top cells are tied; an unchanged-recipe replay scores 0.9228 > baseline 0.887, so noise lets null patches earn sigma about 0.127; the visible proxy is a misaligned unbounded NLL diagnostic; and the candidate tokenizer/chat template is trusted unhashed by the scorer (latent, not observed).
